It could be that at some points in time, as in the case of Bonic, some of the arrested HVO would remain there until transfer to the prison in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Eminovic. Ideally - and I agree with you - ideally that was the purpose of the detention centre; ideally. But realistically now, could you tell the Court what transpired at that centre.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, actually, I have no information as to what was going on at this centre. I said that I was there for the first time in the case of Bonic. And as far as I can remember, I may have been there one more time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: With the permission of the Trial Chamber, Mr. President, I'd wish to show the witness Prosecution Exhibit P40, please. Mr. President, Your Honours, it's on Sanction at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document is marked under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Could we just show it on the monitor for now? Is that -- that should be sufficient. And I believe we'll have to go into private session for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we shall go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution has noted the objections of the counsel for Defence. The fact that you were not -- clarified -- some points, and neither were we, and we asked that some of his military functions be clarified. He doesn't want to tell us some elements, and I think it is useless to continue to ask further questions because the witness does not want to elaborate on his military functions. I asked him the questions and it was said that he had been assisting Mr. Salko Beba. Well, perhaps we will have to hear Mr. Beba subsequently. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. President, we'll have to hear Mr. Beba subsequently, but perhaps we can also take another route. And I think my friend is being very unfair to me when she said that in examination-in-chief I couldn't put it - not that I couldn't put it -- not that I didn't - I couldn't, because the witness wouldn't allow me. So I think the point has come now when, Mr. President and Your Honours, that we the Prosecution will have to deem this witness a hostile witness to be able to get the evidence to the Court as is -- as is from his report and from his statement. So we wish to make an application now to deem this witness a hostile witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We ask the witness to leave the courtroom so that the Prosecution can elaborate on its requests.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now in the stage when the Prosecution wishes for us to take note of the fact that this witness is a hostile witness. What are the elements? What are the grounds on the basis of which you are embarking upon this road?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, the only way I can achieve the evidence as -- that we had before us and that the witness had given to us would be by this route, because as my learned friend indicated, I would have proofed the witness and I would have known. But there was no way for me to bring it before the Court other than this way, to let the Court know what happened at the proofing. If the Court would have recognised this morning, I was faced with great difficulty in getting this witness to answer and answer accurately. He was very, very hesitant in his responses, and the examination-in-chief had to be curtailed for the very reason. In the proofing, the witness indicated to us evidence that was exactly opposite to what he has come here this afternoon and said. With respect to the Travnik barracks, he told us about the HVO prisoners being detained, about how many prisoners were kept in a cell, about the beatings, and this afternoon he comes to the Court and he says to the Tribunal here that he never heard about the beatings, he never knew of anything. He talks -- he told us in proofing, when he was shown the orders, that he knew nothing of these orders. And, Mr. President, as we speak I'm trying to get copies of the orders -- oh, my learned friend just has indicated to me that they have arrived. There are orders here - and I questioned him on the orders, and he said to me he had no part in the making of orders. He did not do orders; he did not carry out orders; he was not a part of it. And the orders clearly said instructions that were given to him and they were given to him and his name was mentioned in the orders. And he denied it. Yet when my friend produced orders, he affirmed it; he said yes, he knew about the orders. He talked in his evidence about Bonic, and he refused to go on to elaborate what he knew else, and all that was told to him about other witnesses. And he insists and he tries to -- rather, to be untruthful to the Court by letting -- by giving the Court the impression that his military duties were not of a particular way, as well as in his -- in the orders and in his statement he said otherwise. He said at first that he was never a military officer. Then he comes here and he says, "Yes, I'm a military officer." One minute he's civilian; the next minute he changes his clothes to military. And for this purpose, Mr. President, Your Honours, I think that the witness should be confronted with his statement, confronted with the proofing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, the motion to have this witness declared a hostile witness is an important act by the party calling a witness. It is their own witness who is obliged to tell the whole truth before this Chamber. The standard that needs to be met to -- for a witness to be declared hostile - and one must say that this is the first case in this Chamber - is one that was very rarely used. The standard has to be very high. One needs to demonstrate to this Chamber in what respect the witness is hostile to the party producing him. However, all that is being shown to you today, Mr. President, is that the witness was difficult during the examination-in-chief, and this is not sufficient, Mr. President. We are told that he didn't tell this Chamber the whole truth during -- in relation to the proofing session. However, we have the previous statement of this witness and we do not see any marked difference between what the witness said today and what can be found in the statement. Of course the same words are not used. But if my learned friend from the Prosecution wishes to produce the statement, paragraph 14, the witness said such-and-such a thing to the investigator, and then he can respond. And that is why I wish to cross-examine him. It is such a test, a demonstration of this kind can lead to a declaration of hostility. But to say that the witness gave different answers during a proofing session with the Prosecution, that goes to the credibility of the witness, which the Chamber can judge. The Chamber has the opportunity to question the witness. We have done the cross-examination. There was an examination-in-chief and a long re-examination. We have an idea of what this witness can and cannot contribute. But we have to go back to some of his answers. The witness spoke of his military role. The witness did say what he did with Mr. Beba regarding transports. He drafted orders. What was the military component of his work? He never refused to answer a question regarding the military nature of his work. He also provided certain clarifications, saying that at the same time he worked for the commission and as an assistant to Mr. Beba. He also explained why he worked for Mr. Beba: Because the personnel attached to Mr. Beba were inadequate and we are in the middle of the war; everyone is working 20 hours a day, he has two employees, and that is why he was needed. He explained that. He told us what he knew about the prisoners. And in our opinion, there are no major differences between his testimony and his prior statement. All these reasons, we believe that the Prosecution has not attained the necessary standard to have this witness declared a hostile one. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other Defence counsel? Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. We have no further observations, other than those already made by Mr. Bourgon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber will withdraw for a few minutes, and we will come back to give our ruling. --- Break taken at 12.36 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber is going to render its ruling regarding the motion of the Prosecution for the Chamber to declare this witness hostile, and as a result they would present to the witness his written statement, as well as all other necessary documents. The Chamber noted that the Defence opposed this, explaining that there was no reason to consider this witness to be hostile. In view of the importance of the problem raised, the Chamber is of the opinion that it would be best to adjourn the hearing for today so that the Chamber may render its decision tomorrow at 9.00. So we are going to bring the witness back in to tell him that he has to stay and appear again tomorrow morning. At this stage there's no room for any further interventions, because our decision will be rendered tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Eminovic, you have been asked to leave the courtroom because a procedural problem arose, and this is a problem that we have to address and we will deal with it tomorrow when we resume work at 9.00; which unfortunately for you will mean that you will have to stay here this afternoon and this evening and to come back tomorrow at 9.00. So do what is necessary to make sure that you are present here at 9.00 to continue your testimony. I would like to ask Madam Usher to accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President -- Mr. President, prior to the witness being --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a moment. The Prosecution has something to say before you leave. Yes, Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: There's one issue. The witness may be told by the Trial Chamber, namely, that he's not allowed to talk to any of the parties in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that goes without saying. But it's better to be specific. Between now and tomorrow you mustn't be in touch with anyone. No one may contact you until tomorrow morning, when you appear here. You may leave now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I have already said, we will render our ruling tomorrow at 9.00, when we begin the hearing. Now I'm going to adjourn. But Mr. Bourgon has something to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Quickly. Will the Chamber be requiring written arguments? Also, Mr. President, can we get additional information regarding the scheduling of witnesses following the discussion we had yesterday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Concerning the schedule, the Prosecution explained what it intended to do, but I'll give them the floor once again regarding the schedule, please. And I must add that this witness will come back tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: For this purpose, Mr. President, can we please go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let's go into private Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. session.
